root_cause.text: The error path in blkcg_maybe_throttle_current() fails to release the disk reference acquired via get_device() when blkcg lookup, blkg lookup, or blkg_tryget() operations fail, because the put_disk() call was inadvertently omitted during the refactoring from request_queue to gendisk.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `put_disk(disk);` to the `out:` label error path that is reached when lookups fail. The commit message explicitly states that "blk_put_queue() in the original code but was inadvertently dropped during the conversion from request_queue to gendisk" (commit f05837ed73d0), and that "current->throttle_disk is already set to NULL before the lookup, blkcg_exit() cannot release this reference either, causing the disk to never be freed." The missing put_disk() call creates a reference leak where the disk object acquired by blkcg_schedule_throttle() is never released on error paths.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function blkcg_maybe_throttle_current() (lines 1719-1751) acquires a disk reference via blk_get_queue(q) implicitly through current->throttle_queue being set by blkcg_schedule_throttle(). However, examining the error paths: when blkcg lookup fails (line 1738 'if (!blkcg)'), when blkg lookup fails (line 1740 'if (!blkg)'), or when blkg_try_get() fails (line 1742 'if (!blkg)'), the code jumps to the 'out:' label at line 1748. At this point, blk_put_queue(q) is called at line 1749 to release the reference. However, the vulnerable construct is that the code does NOT call put_disk() - it only calls blk_put_queue(). The root cause states the fix requires put_disk() to be called in error paths, but this commit only has blk_put_queue(q) at line 1749. The successful path (lines 1743-1747) also only calls blk_put_queue(q) at line 1747, not put_disk(). This indicates the refactoring from request_queue to gendisk was incomplete - the put_disk() call is missing from both the error path and the normal path, representing the bug-introducing commit where the disk reference is acquired but not properly released.
